results.title: Tips to Pinpoint Contamination in Your Extraction Workflow for GC-MS | Biotage
results.content: ### Sample extraction and clean-up. # Tips to Pinpoint Contamination in Your Extraction Workflow for GC-MS. If you see contamination present within your instrument blanks, then you’ll want to give your instrument a good clean-up with fresh supplies. If your instrument blanks are clean, then you’ll want to check your extraction solvents. Place the full volume of fresh extraction solvents into your concentration instrument and concentrate the solvent using your normal parameters. This will be more representative of the amount of contamination that is introduced when using the full volume of extraction solvents within your procedure. If you find that there’s contamination here, then you’ll want to double check the grade of solvent that you’re using. If you are using solvent phase separation paper, then ensure that the paper and apparatus is also cleaned in preparation of drying your extract.

# The Role of Peptide Sequencing in Proteomics Research. One of the most pivotal methods in this realm is **peptide sequencing**, which provides critical insights into protein composition and biological processes. As proteomics continues to drive breakthroughs in drug discovery, disease diagnostics, and biomarker identification, **peptide sequencing** has become indispensable for modern research. In this blog, we’ll explore **the importance of peptide sequencing**, its role in proteomics, and the advanced techniques that enable accurate protein analysis. ### What is Peptide Sequencing? Peptide sequencing is the process of determining the **amino acid sequence** of a peptide or protein. **Why is Peptide Sequencing Important?**. ### Peptide Sequencing and Its Role in Proteomics. Peptide sequencing plays a **foundational role** in proteomics by providing:. ### Techniques Used in Peptide Sequencing. Several advanced techniques form the backbone of peptide sequencing. Mass spectrometry is the **gold standard** for peptide sequencing due to its sensitivity and ability to analyze complex samples. * **Tandem Mass Spectrometry (MS/MS)**: Fragmentation of peptides to determine amino acid sequences. * **Bottom-Up Proteomics**: Proteins are digested into peptides before sequencing. Modern peptide sequencing relies heavily on **bioinformatics** to analyze and interpret complex MS data. These tools enable researchers to match observed peptide fragments with known sequences, identify modifications, and build protein profiles. ### Applications of Peptide Sequencing in Proteomics. Peptide sequencing aids in characterizing **therapeutic targets**, validating drug efficacy, and analyzing protein-drug interactions. Sequencing facilitates the development of **monoclonal antibodies** and peptide-based drugs for targeted therapies. By analyzing protein expression and modifications, peptide sequencing sheds light on molecular mechanisms underlying diseases like cancer and autoimmune disorders. ### Challenges in Peptide Sequencing. ### How ResolveMass Laboratories Supports Peptide Sequencing. Peptide sequencing is a cornerstone of proteomics research, offering deep insights into protein structure, function, and interactions. By enabling biomarker discovery, therapeutic advancements, and disease mechanism studies, peptide sequencing continues to revolutionize the field of life sciences. **ResolveMass Laboratories** stands at the forefront of proteomics innovation, delivering cutting-edge peptide sequencing solutions for diverse applications. 2. results.title: How to Avoid Contamination in Lab Samples
results.content: # How to Avoid Contamination in Lab Samples. Perhaps the most common factor is the contamination of lab samples. Contamination can occur during various points in the lab process. However, there are measures you can take and protocols you can establish to reduce this risk and avoid contamination in lab samples. ## What is contamination? Contamination is when an unwanted substance is present. # How to reduce contamination in the lab. Perhaps the best way to avoid contamination in lab samples is by automating certain aspects of the process. Introducing automated liquid handling equipment into your laboratory can significantly reduce the risk of human error and cross-contamination of samples. For more information regarding the benefits of automated liquid handling and it can help reduce contamination and human error in your lab, check out our helpful beginner’s guide. When you are transferring samples it is critical to work in an environment where the air will not interfere with your sample.

results.title: Cross-laboratory replication of pseudomyxoma peritonei tumor microbiome reveals reproducible microbial signatures | mSphere
results.content:
Title: Cross-laboratory replication of pseudomyxoma peritonei tumor microbiome reveals reproducible microbial signatures | mSphere
A subset of PMP tumors and NP samples that appeared to sequence robustly (i.e., >1,000 sequencing reads and >100 mg remaining tissue) were then selected from lab 1 for independent DNA extraction and sequencing replication in lab 2 (Fig. 1A). With both lab 1 and 2 data sets, we then focused on high-quality tumor and control tissue samples by developing a stepwise filtering approach, which aimed to identify and remove samples with poor quality and perceived gross bacterial contamination from our downstream analysis (Fig. 1B). Following quality filtering, the 21 PMP tumors retained 5,670 sequences per sample on average (range: 749–33,825) (Fig. 1C; Table S3). After the second contamination filter, seven of these nine PMP tumors and both NP control tissue samples passed (Fig. 1B). To evaluate whether our filtering criteria identified low-quality samples with gross background contamination, we visualized the PMP and NP tissue samples along with their respective negative controls using a Bray-Curtis principal coordinate analysis (PCoA) (Fig. 2A and B). We hypothesized that high-quality sample extractions are likely to contain reproducible tumor-associated microbial features while low-quality sample replicates with low reads and/or gross contamination will have few to no features in common. However, for PMP-433, which was considered “High/High” (e.g., two high-quality extractions), we were able to detect the most abundant taxa across all additional replicates, demonstrating that at least in this case, the microbial community within a small (~200 mg) sample of tumor seems homogenous (Fig. S4). We were surprised to find that several NP samples resulted in high-quality DNA extractions, including one sample with 20 reproducible ASVs. Of the core set of bacterial genera present in 40%–70% of all high-quality tumor extractions*—Staphylococcus*, *Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Corynebacterium,* and *Streptococcus*—all but *Streptococcus* and *Acinetobacter* were present and reproducible across NP-24 (although in low relative abundance). We identified multiple bacterial taxa that are likely tumor associated owing to their reproducibility across independently extracted and sequenced samples, their presence in other high-quality PMP tumors, and their absence from control tissues (Tables 1 and 2). Global contaminant ASVs (*Escherichia-Shigella, Enterococcus*, and *Brevibacterium*) that were found in the negative control samples across both laboratories were removed from the high-quality PMP tumor extractions prior to identifying core features.
